reference: Peter Cundall and Otto Strack, 'A discrete numerical model for granular assemblies', Geotechnique 29, 47 (1979), gave the distinct element method used here: rigid disks, a linear normal spring with a dashpot, a tangential spring capped by Coulomb friction, and an explicit step bounded by the contact period. The settle is not time-accurate at its production step: the restitution coefficient depends on where in a step contact begins, −12.1% to +5.7% of the analytic value at damping ≤ 0.5 (the pre-registered 10% bound was missed); it converges at first order to the analytic contact law.

The top load does not load the packing: at photo, strong and slip the lid carries at most 3.4% of the weight at any step and nothing at the end, so presets with a top load, and the periodic sides only they use, are outside the domain.

The starting lattice overlaps (255 to 562 pairs, up to 1.29 r0), so every packing is prepared by an explosive decompression and settling, not a pour. The same seed settles to a different packing in Node and Chromium because Math.cos differs by one ulp between them; each engine reprints its own packing exactly.

No Radjai force-distribution, Janssen, photoelastic or experimental claim: side-wall friction carries −6.2% to +7.0% of the weight depending on history, and the column preset carries −0.1% in its printed packing. Broader settings require additional independent evidence.

numerical.criteria: Fixed before the first run and committed first. Collisions: e and contact duration within 0.5% of the no-tension analytic values at h/64 in every case; refinement to h/64 reduces the e error tenfold or below 0.1%; e within 10% at the production step for damping ≤ 0.5; the tensile formula off by more than ten times the clamped error at damping ≥ 0.2; e identical (1e-9) across hardness. Friction: displacements within 1%, stick time within 2% plus two steps, no slip beyond the elastic range of the tangential spring after sticking or below the incline threshold, total slip within 3% above it, |J_t/J_n| and the slip change within 2% of μ and 3J_t/m_eff. Statics: vertical and horizontal wall balance within 1% of the floor load, dashpot share of the normal forces below 1%, kinetic energy below the module's at-rest threshold, contacts, backbone and Z identical and the other status quantities within 1e-12 of a brute-force rebuild; Z bands [3.8, 4.6], [3.0, 4.0], [2.8, 3.6] at friction 0, 0.4, 0.8, separated by more than 3 standard errors; column side walls carry more than 5% of the weight. Misses (production e for rmin–rmax at damping 0.5, −10.6%; incline slip at tan θ/3μ = 1.05, +8.7% at every friction) are recorded and reproduced exactly; follow-ups with criteria fixed before they ran test their causes.
numerical.benchmark: The linear spring–dashpot with the F_n ≥ 0 clamp has e = exp(−ζω0 t_c), ω_d t_c = π − 2 asin ζ (Schwager and Pöschel, Granular Matter 9, 465 (2007)); rigid-disk Coulomb friction with I = m r²/2 (sliding to rolling, the incline threshold tan θ = 3μ, and impulse theory in gross sliding) including the module's background drag; Newton's static balance of the settled packing against the total weight; isostatic coordination (4 without friction, falling toward 3 with it); a brute-force contact rebuild for the status line.
numerical.failureControl: A flipped dashpot sign (e = 2.475 against 0.404) and a dashpot allowed to pull (e = 0.309, the tensile value) fail the collision criteria; wall friction off, a flipped wall torque, incline friction off and a flipped torque on the second grain of a pair (slip change −66.7%) fail the friction criteria; a settle cut to 5% of its budget (vertical residual 116%), gravity on the mean mass (5.9%) and a Verlet list that is never rebuilt (36165 contacts missing) fail the statics.
numerical.limitations: Contact tests isolate one or two disks through a hand-built D. The production step restitutes within −12.1% to +5.7% of the analytic value over contact phases at damping ≤ 0.5 (swing ≈ 2ζω0h); the undamped tangential spring overshoots the rigid Coulomb slip by an amount scaling as 1/√k_n (8.7% at hardness 4000 just above the threshold) while sustained sliding matches μF_n to 1.4e-4. reference: Oded Schramm, Israel Journal of Mathematics 118, 221 (2000), 'Scaling limits of loop-erased random walks and uniform spanning trees'. Charles Loewner's 1923 equation grows a curve into the upper half plane from a real driving function; Schramm showed that the only conformally invariant random curves with the domain Markov property come from driving it with Brownian motion of variance κ, and identified κ with the critical models whose interfaces they describe. Gregory Lawler, Schramm and Wendelin Werner computed the exponents; Stanislav Smirnov proved the percolation case. The curve is computed here as a composition of vertical slit maps, after Tom Kennedy, Journal of Statistical Physics 137, 839 (2009).

reference: Lionel Levine and Yuval Peres, 'Strong spherical asymptotics for rotor-router aggregation and the divisible sandpile', Potential Analysis 30, 1 (2009), is the theorem this plate measures. For an aggregate of n particles in d dimensions, written as n = ω_d r^d, they prove the inradius is at least r − O(log r) and the outradius at most r + O(r^α) for every α > 1 − 1/d, which in the plane is r + O(r^α) for every α > 1/2. The two sides of that sandwich are not the same strength, and the plate does not pretend they are: the inner bound is logarithmic and proved, the outer bound proved here is a power, and the status line reports what this lattice actually measures rather than what the tighter of the two would suggest. There is no probability anywhere in the statement. The rotor-router walk and the aggregation model are James Propp's; they are studied in Ander Holroyd and James Propp, 'Rotor walks and Markov chains', Contemporary Mathematics 520 (2010), and in Joshua Cooper and Joel Spencer, 'Simulating a random walk with constant error', Combinatorics, Probability and Computing 15 (2006). Internal diffusion limited aggregation, the random counterpart drawn beside it, is Gregory Lawler, Maury Bramson and David Griffeath, 'Internal diffusion limited aggregation', Annals of Probability 20, 2117 (1992), who proved its limit shape is a disk; David Jerison, Lionel Levine and Scott Sheffield, Journal of the American Mathematical Society 25, 271 (2012), showed its fluctuations are logarithmic as well, so the gap the plate measures between the two is one of constants and of certainty, not of orders. That a finished aggregate does not depend on the order the particles were routed in is the abelian property of Persi Diaconis and William Fulton, Rendiconti del Seminario Matematico dell'Università e del Politecnico di Torino (1991); it is the same argument Deepak Dhar, Physical Review Letters 64, 1613 (1990), made for the abelian sandpile of Per Bak, Chao Tang and Kurt Wiesenfeld, Physical Review Letters 59, 381 (1987).

reference: Noam Elkies, Greg Kuperberg, Michael Larsen and James Propp, Journal of Algebraic Combinatorics 1, 111 and 219 (1992), counted the domino tilings of the Aztec diamond of order n (there are 2^{n(n+1)/2}) and gave the shuffling algorithm that samples one uniformly. William Jockusch, James Propp and Peter Shor, 'Random domino tilings and the arctic circle theorem' (1998), proved that a uniformly random tiling is frozen outside the inscribed circle and disordered inside it. James Propp, Theoretical Computer Science 303, 267 (2003), on generalized domino shuffling.
equation: order n → n+1: delete colliding pairs, slide N↑ S↓ W← E→, fill each empty 2×2 block with a random pair
limitations: Since 2026-09-24 the tab's frozen regions are the theorem's polar regions (a domino connected to the boundary through edge-adjacent dominoes of its own type, as Johansson 2005 states the definition of Jockusch, Propp and Shor); they equal an independent union-find on every plate, and the polar fraction extrapolates to 0.2141 +/- 0.0014 against 1 - pi/4 (-0.3 sigma). The earlier local test read 0.2778 +/- 0.0009, 67 sigma high.

The status line's per-plate error bar (the spread of the four polar regions) is conservative: the scatter of the fraction over seeds is 0.68 to 0.98 of it at orders 40 to 320, because the four regions are anticorrelated. It fails the tool's calibration band (0.75 to 1.33, set before the data), so the record stays partially validated. At finite n the printed fraction exceeds the limit by a term that shrinks as n^(-2/3), and the status line says so.

Exact uniformity is established by exhaustive enumeration only at orders 1 to 5, run through the tab's build() and shuffle() below the UI range of 8 to 320; larger orders are tested only through the arctic boundary statistics.

The polar-region area and the axis radius agree with 1 - pi/4 and 1/sqrt(2) only after extrapolation in n with the stated form q_inf + A n^-2/3 + B n^-1 (0.3 and 0.7 sigma); a two-parameter n^-2/3 fit over orders 113 to 320 differs by 2.5 and 3.1 sigma, and at order 320 the polar area is still 0.030 above its limit.
Uniformity probabilities assume the seeded U.makeRng streams behave as independent uniform draws; fixed PRNG samples do not prove it.

reference: Eugene Wigner's semicircle law, Annals of Mathematics 62, 548 (1955), and Freeman Dyson's threefold way and Brownian-motion model, J. Math. Phys. 3, 140 and 1191 (1962). The tridiagonal matrix models that make a general β cheap to sample are Ioana Dumitriu and Alan Edelman, 'Matrix models for beta ensembles', J. Math. Phys. 43, 5830 (2002). The status line compares the spacing spread with the exact Gaudin-Mehta law (Michel Mehta, Random Matrices), evaluated as Fredholm determinants by Folkmar Bornemann's method, Math. Comp. 79, 871 (2010); Wigner's surmise is its 2×2 approximation. The gamma sampler is George Marsaglia and Wai Wan Tsang, ACM TOMS 26, 363 (2000).
equation: p(λ) ∝ ∏_{i<j} |λ_i − λ_j|^β · e^{−Σλ_i²/4};   Dyson (β = 1): dλ_i = √2 dB_i + (Σ_{j≠i} 1/(λ_i − λ_j) − λ_i/2) dt
limitations: Complete evidence covers only the domain in validation/RMT.md: sampler, solver and exact moments for n 24-400 and beta 0.1-12, semicircle for beta 1-12, Gaudin-Mehta spacing law at beta 1 and 2 with n 400, the printed spread of two presets, Dyson mode at 24 paths, and five complete prints.

The code samples the Dumitriu-Edelman matrix without its 1/sqrt(2), so the eigenvalue density is exp(-sum l^2/4); since 2026-09-24 the displayed equation says so, and it shows the Dyson mode's -l/2 Ornstein-Uhlenbeck drift at beta = 1.

At n 150 the local unfolding (24-gap window) biases the spacing scale: the CV agrees with Gaudin-Mehta but the pooled KS distance (0.0043, 0.0044) exceeds its bootstrap critical value (0.0027, 0.0025). The spacing-distribution claim is limited to n 400.

Since 2026-09-24 the status line prints the unfolded CV through compare() with its row-bootstrap error against the exact Gaudin-Mehta values (0.53435 at beta 1, 0.42426 at beta 2), with the Wigner surmise as a note; at beta 1 the tab's own sample resolves the surmise's 0.012 error. Only beta 1 and 2 have an exact reference in the status line.
Finite samples from one seeded PRNG; error bars assume independent draws. Beta 4 spacings, edge statistics, beta outside 0.05-20 and the sweep plate's printed spread are not tested.
The shell's SVG raster differs from the canvas only where ticks overlap (group versus per-mark opacity); since 2026-09-24 the Dyson polylines carry round caps, as the canvas does.

Colour is not evidence. Since 2026-09-24 the ramp no longer wraps its top to its bottom colour at palette offset 0 (the top level and the last row had taken the lowest colour). A nonzero offset rotates the ramp cyclically by 16 of 256 entries per step, so the two ends of the data range take neighbouring colours. No mark moves.

reference: Uche, Stillinger and Torquato, Phys. Rev. E 70, 046122 (2004), and Torquato, Stillinger, Phys. Rev. E 68, 041113 (2003). reference: The sampler is James Propp and David Wilson, 'Exact sampling with coupled Markov chains and applications to statistical mechanics', Random Structures and Algorithms 9, 223 to 252 (1996); random tilings are one of their own worked examples. The limit shape measured on the plate is Henry Cohn, Michael Larsen and James Propp, 'The shape of a typical boxed plane partition', New York Journal of Mathematics 4, 137 to 165 (1998). The count of boxed plane partitions is Percy MacMahon, 'Memoir on the theory of the partitions of numbers, Part VI: partitions in two-dimensional space, to which is added an adumbration of the theory of partitions in three-dimensional space', Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A 211, 345 to 373 (1912). The height function that turns a tiling into a stack of cubes is William Thurston, 'Conway's tiling groups', American Mathematical Monthly 97, 757 to 773 (1990). How long this chain needs is David Wilson, 'Mixing times of lozenge tiling and card shuffling Markov chains', Annals of Applied Probability 14, 274 to 325 (2004).

reference: David Bruce Wilson, 'Generating random spanning trees more quickly than the cover time', Proceedings of the 28th ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing, 296 (1996), is the algorithm drawn here: cycle popping by loop-erased random walk, exact rather than approximate, with the expected cost determined by root-dependent commute times. Those are Andrei Broder, 'Generating random spanning trees', 30th Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science, 442 (1989), and David Aldous, SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics 3, 450 (1990). The loop-erased walk itself is Gregory Lawler, Duke Mathematical Journal 47, 655 (1980). Lawler, Oded Schramm and Wendelin Werner, Annals of Probability 32, 939 (2004), proved that the loop-erased walk scales to SLE with κ = 2 and the tree's Peano curve to SLE with κ = 8. That every spanning tree of a graph can be counted at all is Gustav Kirchhoff, Annalen der Physik 148, 497 (1847).
equation: pick v ∉ T, walk at random from v erasing each loop as it closes, attach the surviving path;  P(T) = 1 / κ(G) for every one of the κ(G) spanning trees

reference: W. P. Su, J. R. Schrieffer and A. J. Heeger, Phys. Rev. Lett. 42, 1698 (1979), on dimerised polyacetylene. The winding of the Bloch Hamiltonian in the Brillouin zone is a topological invariant; when it is 1 an open chain hosts a zero mode at each end, inside the bulk gap. Periodic boundaries have nowhere to put them. The plate is |ψ_n(x)|² of every eigenmode of the finite chain, energy increasing upward, each row scaled to its own peak; the mid-gap pair sits in the middle rows.
equation: H = v Σ_i (a†_i b_i + h.c.) + w Σ_i (b†_i a_{i+1} + h.c.),   ν = 1 for w > v (open)
limitations: The studio solver is compared with an independent Float64 Jacobi solve on every registered preset (N = 96, and Critical at N = 160). Other grids, the plate's row mapping, per-row scaling and palette, and the print path are not compared pixel by pixel. No interactions or experiment.

The end weight and the verdict are measured from the eigenvectors of one finite chain and carry no sampling error; they are finite-size quantities with a fixed 10% window at each end. Mid-gap energies under 1e-13 are not resolved in double precision and are printed as a bound. Critical (w/v 1.06) reads crossover at the default 96 sites, because its localisation length of 18.5 cells is comparable to the 48-cell chain; at 160 sites it reads edge modes.

Until 2026-09-24 the intra hopping was keyed v, which the engine overwrites with the recipe version (2). Every plate opened from a hash, a preset, Surprise or a reload therefore ran at v = 2 and drew the trivial picture whatever the controls said. Dragging the slider changed the plate on screen, but its hash still recorded only v = 2. The key is now vIntra. A hash written before the rename never stored the intra hopping, so it reprints at the default 0.45 with its stored w, and its pixels change.
Finite open/periodic chains only; catalog equation and citation remain review targets for full paper equivalence.

reference: Per Bak, Chao Tang and Kurt Wiesenfeld, Phys. Rev. Lett. 59, 381 (1987); Deepak Dhar, Phys. Rev. Lett. 64, 1613 (1990). Bak, Tang and Wiesenfeld dropped grains one at a time on a lattice with a toppling threshold and found avalanches of every size, a power law with no tuning: self-organized criticality. Dhar showed the toppling operators commute, so the final stable state does not depend on the order of toppling, and the recurrent configurations form an Abelian group. The identity of that group, computed on a square, is the fractal plate in the second mode.
equation: if hᵢ ≥ 4: hᵢ −= 4, hⱼ += 1 for each neighbor j;   identity e = (2m − (2m)°)°, m = all 3
limitations: Complete evidence covers only the finite domain in validation/SANDPILE.md: square n x n grids with the tab's sink boundary, exhaustive recurrent counts up to 3x3, the identity at 64, 96, 128, 192 and 256, the six menu grain counts of the single-source pile, two random-drop runs and six printed recipes.
The recurrent count does not detect a threshold raised to five while toppling still removes four grains (that model is the sandpile shifted by one grain); the stability range check does.

Fixed 2026-09-24: the status line's topplings and random-drop avalanche numbers counted pops of floor(h/4) topplings (and, for the single-source pile, only the octant's own cells), so they undercounted and depended on toppling order. They now count topplings, the order-independent odometer total, and tools/sandpile-science.js checks every printed number exactly against independent odometers, with the pre-fix counter as a failure control; the plates are unchanged. Avalanche-size statistics and self-organized-criticality exponents are not tested.

Print evidence is raster PNG through Chromium with a software renderer; pixels within 0.01 cell of a cell boundary may show the neighboring cell (fixed-point scaling), and other renderers are not covered.

reference: S. R. Broadbent and J. M. Hammersley, Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 53, 629 (1957); J. Hoshen and R. Kopelman, Phys. Rev. B 14, 3438 (1976); Harry Kesten, Comm. Math. Phys. 74, 41 (1980). Broadbent and Hammersley asked how a fluid spreads through a random porous medium and found a sharp threshold: below p_c every cluster is finite, above it one cluster spans the lattice. Kesten proved the bond threshold on the square lattice is exactly 1/2. The site threshold, about 0.592746, is known only numerically. Hoshen and Kopelman gave the one-pass labeling that finds the clusters.
equation: site occupied iff rᵢ < p;   bond open iff rᵢⱼ < p;   p_c(site) ≈ 0.5927,   p_c(bond) = 1/2

reference: K. Weierstrass, presented to the Prussian Academy in 1872 (published 1875). Analysts had assumed a continuous function was differentiable except at isolated points; Weierstrass wrote a Fourier series that is continuous everywhere and differentiable nowhere. Each finite sum is smooth; the classical infinite-series theorem is not established for this displayed field.

reference: A. Yu. Kitaev, Phys.-Usp. 44, 131 (2001). A 1D p-wave superconductor hosts two Majorana operators, one at each end, that together make a single nonlocal fermion. They sit at zero energy, inside the gap, and are their own antiparticles. The plate is computed: the 2N × 2N Bogoliubov-de Gennes matrix of an open chain of N sites, one per column, is diagonalized exactly in double precision (Householder reduction and implicit QL, after Wilkinson and Reinsch, 1971), and each row is |u(x)|² + |v(x)|² of one ± pair of quasiparticle modes, scaled to its own peak, on a linear |E| axis from zero at the top.
equation: H = −μ Σ c†c − t Σ (c†_i c_{i+1}+h.c.) + Δ Σ (c_i c_{i+1}+h.c.),   |μ|<2t ⇒ unpaired γ_L, γ_R
limitations: Complete evidence covers the finite domain in validation/KITAEV.md: mean-field BdG Kitaev chains of 96 to 160 sites in the studio (the grids the tab allows), open in the tab and periodic or antiperiodic in the band check; shorter chains only in the Node tests of the module code.

Splittings below about 4Nε‖H‖ (1e-13 to 4e-13) are not resolved by double precision and are flagged; for most topological presets the exact splitting is far below that. An exact finite-N splitting is used only at Δ = t; elsewhere the rate and oscillation are tested, not the prefactor.
No self-consistent Δ, interactions, disorder, spin or nanowire experiment.
remaining: An exact finite-N splitting for general Δ (for example the closed forms of Leumer et al., J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 32, 445502, 2020) would turn the rate test into a value test.

reference: V. G. Veselago, Sov. Phys. Usp. 10, 509 (1968), asked what optics would do if ε and μ were both negative: a left-handed medium, a reversed Doppler shift, and a slab that acts as a lens. reference: Ernst Ising, Z. Phys. 31, 253 (1925); Lars Onsager, Phys. Rev. 65, 117 (1944); Nicholas Metropolis, Arianna W. Rosenbluth, Marshall N. Rosenbluth, Augusta H. Teller and Edward Teller, J. Chem. Phys. 21, 1087 (1953). Ising solved the chain and found no transition. Onsager solved the square lattice exactly and found one at T_c = 2/ln(1+√2). The Metropolis algorithm samples the Boltzmann distribution by proposing single flips and accepting them with probability min(1, exp(−ΔE/T)). Here the lattice is updated as a checkerboard: two half-sweeps per step, each parity with its neighbors held fixed, so the GPU can flip every site of one color at once.

reference: Three-vortex collapse bound: an explicit formula and sharp minimum for a classical three-vortex collapse family, independently derived in this project with AI assistance. Circulations Γ = (1, 1, −1/2), positions z₁ = 0, z₂ = 1, z₃ = 1/2 + (√3/2) e^{iθ} on the L = 0 circle, 0 < θ < π/2. θ is the third vortex's place on that circle, not an interior angle. ω₀ t_c = (2 − cos²θ)/sin(2θ) ≥ √2, equality uniquely at tan θ = 1/√2 (interior angles 22.5°, 45°, 112.5°). With u = tan θ the product is u + 1/(2u), and ω₀ t_c − √2 = (√2 u − 1)² / (2u) ≥ 0. At θ = 45° the product is 3/2. Three-vortex collapse is Gröbli (1877). Aref, Phys. Fluids 22, 057104 (2010), gives rotation and collapse separately and writes their product as the pitch of the log spiral. The formula explicitly specializes and reparameterizes the spiral coefficient in Gröbli (1877), section 10. Kimura, J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. 56, 2024 (1987), section 4, gives the collapse and rotation rates A and B in this same parametrization, for circulations (2, 2, −1), and their ratio B/(−2A) is this formula; he minimizes the collision time instead, at cos 2θ = 3/5, where the product is 3/2, the value it also takes at θ = 45°. It was independently derived here and recorded on 2026-09-19. Priority of the optimized minimum remains unconfirmed; see identities/ORIGINALITY-FOLLOWUP.md, identities/NOVELTY-AUDIT.md and IDENTITIES.md. Cite as Three-vortex collapse bound. If the vortices leave the circle, or the kernel is wrong, the ratio against √2 misses and the status line marks miss. The picture still draws.
equation: ω₀ t_c = (2 − cos²θ)/sin(2θ) ≥ √2  on  Γ = (1, 1, −1/2), L = 0;  equality at tan θ = 1/√2

reference: A closed form and sharp minimum for the scale-invariant product on the classical four-vortex parallelogram collapse family, independently derived in this project with AI assistance. Circulations Γ = (1, 1, −2 − √3, −2 − √3), diagonals in ratio √(2 + √3), angle θ between the diagonals, 0 < θ < π/2. ω₀ t_c = (√3/4)(4 − cos 2θ)/sin(2θ) ≥ 3√5/4, equality uniquely at cos 2θ = 1/4. With φ = 2θ the quotient is (4 − cos φ)/sin φ, and the critical point is cos φ = 1/4. Four-vortex parallelogram collapse is Novikov and Sedov, Sov. Phys. JETP 50, 297 (1979). Gotoda, arXiv:2002.09624 (2020 preprint), eq. (3.13), gives the collapse rate A(θ) and the spin B(θ) separately after those authors. The product −B/(2A) simplifies to the formula above. The formula and minimum were derived here and recorded on 2026-09-20. Historical priority is unconfirmed; see identities/NOVELTY-AUDIT.md and IDENTITIES.md. The reciprocal pair Γ = (1, 1, −2 + √3, −2 + √3) is the same family with the diagonals swapped. If the vortices leave the parallelogram, or the kernel is wrong, the ratio against 3√5/4 misses and the status line marks miss. The picture still draws.
equation: ω₀ t_c = (√3/4)(4 − cos 2θ)/sin(2θ) ≥ 3√5/4  on the Novikov–Sedov parallelogram;  equality at cos 2θ = 1/4

reference: A closed form and sharp minimum for the scale-invariant product on a classical five-vortex collapse family, independently derived in this project with AI assistance. Circulations Γ = (−1, −1, 1/2, 1/2, −3/4), four vortices at the vertices of a parallelogram whose diagonals meet at the fifth, diagonals in ratio 1/√2, angle θ between the diagonals, 0 < θ < π/2. ω₀ t_c = (3/16)(7 − 4 cos 2θ)/sin(2θ) ≥ 3√33/16, equality uniquely at cos 2θ = 4/7. With φ = 2θ the quotient is (7 − 4 cos φ)/sin φ, and the critical point is cos φ = 4/7. Five-vortex parallelogram-plus-center collapse is Novikov and Sedov, Sov. Phys. JETP 50, 297 (1979). Gotoda, arXiv:2002.09624 (2020 preprint), eq. (3.13), gives the collapse rate A(θ) and the spin B(θ) separately after those authors, and plots this family (γ1 = −1, γ2 = 1/2, γ3 = −3/4) as Hamiltonian against collapse rate. The product −B/(2A) on that slice simplifies to the formula above. The formula and minimum were derived here and recorded on 2026-09-20. Historical priority is unconfirmed; see identities/NOVELTY-AUDIT.md and IDENTITIES.md. The reciprocal pair with the diagonals swapped is the same family. If the vortices leave the quincunx, or the kernel is wrong, the ratio against 3√33/16 misses and the status line marks miss. The picture still draws. This is not Novikov and Sedov's t_* or ω separately under a new name, and it is not the four-vortex parallelogram lock.
equation: ω₀ t_c = (3/16)(7 − 4 cos 2θ)/sin(2θ) ≥ 3√33/16  on the Novikov–Sedov five-vortex quincunx;  equality at cos 2θ = 4/7

reference: Classical two-ring collapse: Aref, Physics of Fluids 25, 2183 (1982); Koiller, Pinto de Carvalho, Rodrigues da Silva and Gonçalves de Oliveira, Physica D 16, 27–61 (1985), §11. Two regular n-gons with outer circulation −1, inner circulation x = (n + √(2n−1))/(n−1), and squared radius ratio x. GENChase derives the product and its sharp minimum in identities/polygon-collapse.md. The n = 4 value √322/9 illustrates the general theorem. Historical priority of these explicit bounds is unconfirmed; the collapse family is classical.
equation: ω₀t_c = (K_n − √(2n−1) cos nθ)/(2n sin nθ) ≥ F_n; F₃ = √29/3, F₄ = √322/9

domain.resolution: Trajectory error<1e-6, independent refinement<1e-8, SVG coordinate error<1e-9 pixels, raster/vector mean difference<1.5 bytes, exact state preserved. Exact grid, trajectory times and print dimensions are recorded with each case.
domain.precision: Binary64 numerical references and solver coordinates; Float32 fields where present; RGBA8 PNG and declared SVG decimal precision. Reference refinements and renderer environment recorded.

reference: Classical scalar wave equation. Centered finite differences and the three-dimensional CFL bound follow H. P. Langtangen and S. Linge, Finite Difference Computing with PDEs (2017), wave equation chapter, https://hplgit.github.io/fdm-book/doc/pub/wave/html/._wave-solarized004.html. No novelty or full acoustic model is claimed.
equation: ∂²u/∂t² = c²(∂²u/∂x² + ∂²u/∂y² + ∂²u/∂z²)
limitations: Periodic unit-cube constant-speed scalar wave only; prepared Fourier modes; no full acoustic/EM/elastic material model. Float64 twin long-time through 96³/1200 and 128³ short fixture; GPU atlas remains short-time ≤80 steps on grids ≤64.
Selected exports preserve field and dimensions; physical color calibration and full print-resolution fidelity remain unvalidated.
remaining: Pulse continuum error, extreme 192–256 GPU allocation, and cross-device behavior before generalizing beyond prepared modes.
Independent print-resolution / orientation fidelity beyond the registered small export states.

numerical.scope: Actual float32 atlas shader: four discrete Fourier fixtures, independent float64 mixed-field comparison, fixed-domain/time 16/32/64 combined refinement and 84 sanitizer cases.
numerical.criteria: Maximum solver error below 5e-5, separate native GPU trig initializer error below 3e-4, refinement ratios in [3.5,4.5], maximum sanitized CFL fraction 0.95.
numerical.limitations: Grids 16 through 64 and at most 80 steps; no extreme-grid, long-time, arbitrary-control, cross-device or experimental accuracy claim.
numerical.benchmark: Closed solution of the discrete seven-point Fourier symbol; independent float64 seven-point recurrence; exact continuum standing wave at fixed unit cube and final time 0.13.
numerical.failureControl: Reversing the Laplacian sign gives maximum error above 0.1; Nyquist mode at 1.05 CFL grows above 1e6 while 0.95 CFL remains below 1.0001.

numerical.scope: Node Float64 twin of the seven-point leapfrog: long-time discrete modal phase/frequency fidelity at grids 32–96³ (400–1200 steps), continuum dispersion RMS under 32/48/64/96 refinement at fixed T=0.25, and a 128³ short discrete fixture.
numerical.criteria: Discrete long-time field max below 5e-5 and relative θ error below 1e-10; continuum RMS shrinks under refinement with 96³ RMS below 1/4 of 32³; wrong Courant in analytic θ and reverse Laplacian each exceed max error 0.1.
numerical.limitations: Float64 twin of prepared Fourier modes only; not a GPU float32/SwiftShader long-time campaign, pulse continuum, arbitrary-control, cross-device or print-accuracy certificate. Combined space/time continuum trend only.
numerical.benchmark: Exact discrete dispersion sin(θ/2)²=(ν²/3)Σsin(π m_j/N)² with standing-wave cos(θ steps)φ; continuum standing wave cos(2π|m|T)φ on the unit cube.
numerical.failureControl: Claiming θ from Courant 0.5 while evolving at 0.8 yields field max above 0.1 and phase gap above 1 after 400 steps; reversing the Laplacian yields field max above 0.1 within 40 steps.

print.scope: Production instance, five presets at grid 32, 8 to 24 steps, XY/XZ/YZ slices, 512x384 exports from a 256x256 canvas. Same-seed field regeneration also checked.
print.criteria: Requested dimensions, fifth-to-95th-percentile luminance span above 5, exact raw field equality before/after export, exact repeated field on the same renderer.
print.limitations: One seed and diagnostic palette, one grid, small print dimensions and one renderer. No physical calibration or broad print fidelity claim.

domain.parameters: Periodic unit-cube constant-speed scalar wave with zero initial velocity; Float64 seven-point leapfrog twin. Long-time discrete modes on grids 32–96³ (400–1200 steps, Courant 0.7–0.85), continuum dispersion at T=0.25 under 32/48/64/96 refinement, 128³ short discrete fixture, plus the short GPU atlas fixtures in volume-wave-science.json.
domain.conditions: Prepared single Fourier standing modes only; discrete dispersion sin(θ/2)²=(ν²/3)Σsin(π m_j/N)² and continuum cos(2π|m|T)φ references; wrong-Courant-in-θ and reverse-Laplacian controls must reject (max error ≫0.1). Print/export checks as registered in the science harness for stated presets.
domain.resolution: Discrete long-time field max ~1e-14 (criteria <5e-5) with relative θ error ~1e-15; continuum RMS 6.56e-3→7.22e-4 (32→96 @ T=0.25); 128³ short discrete max ~6e-15. Exact grids/modes/steps recorded.
domain.precision: Float64 twin of the discrete stencil; not a GPU float32/SwiftShader long-time or cross-device certificate. Combined space/time continuum trend only. Extreme 192–256 GPU allocation unaudited.

reference: Newton, Principia (1687); Verlet, Physical Review 159 (1967), 98. Plummer softening and the direct all-pairs kernel: Nyland, Harris and Prins, GPU Gems 3, chapter 31 (2007). This implementation runs the pair kernel on the CPU.
equation: a_i = Σ(j≠i) m_j (r_j−r_i) / (|r_j−r_i|²+ε²)^(3/2), G=1; velocity Verlet
limitations: Planar Plummer-softened G=1 only. Large-N evidence is force-kernel agreement at fixed snapshots, not a statistical N-body convergence study; dt/ε band is finite-time energy drift on one N=64 disk seed.
Browser cancellation and selected exports preserve a completed-step snapshot — not full scientific print certification across hardware.
remaining: Galaxy equilibrium, unsoftened close encounters and long-time chaotic accuracy remain outside the registered evidence.
Compare scientific state and print geometry at additional dimensions, seeds and hardware.

numerical.scope: Actual production force and velocity-Verlet generators, equal-mass softened circular orbit, unequal-mass five-body conservation and batching equivalence.
numerical.criteria: Finest circular position error below 3e-5, refinement ratio 15 to 17, energy drift below 1e-8; five-body force/momentum residuals below 1e-14/1e-13 and energy drift below 1e-5.
numerical.limitations: Small-body finite-time fixtures, not arbitrary stress settings or astrophysical accuracy.
numerical.benchmark: Independent exact softened two-body circular orbit and independent energy/momentum formulas.
numerical.failureControl: A 1% force-coefficient error exceeds 0.01 trajectory error; broken pair reciprocity exceeds 0.001 momentum-production residual.

numerical.scope: Production Float64 force/Verlet kernels vs independent reverse-order all-pairs Plummer reference at N in {256,1024,4096}; multi-dt/eps energy-drift and position self-convergence on a seeded equal-mass disk (N=64).
numerical.criteria: Force max absolute acceleration difference below 1e-12 and relative L2 below 1e-14 at each N; disk relative energy drift below 5e-4 across dt in {0.004,0.002,0.001} and below 2e-3 across eps in {0.06,0.12,0.24}; position RMS refinement ratio vs fine step in 4.5-5.5.
numerical.limitations: Force-kernel snapshot agreement and finite-time moderate-N regime only; not galaxy equilibrium, unsoftened collisions or chaotic long-time accuracy.
numerical.benchmark: Independent Float64 directed all-pairs Plummer accelerations (reverse partner order, Math.pow r^{-3} form) and production equal-mass disk initial conditions via extracted initial/makeRng.
numerical.failureControl: Reference with G=1.01 or eps*1.05 must exceed 1e-4 / 1e-5 max absolute acceleration difference; 1% broken pair reciprocity must produce net force above 1e-4 and disagree with the independent reference.

print.scope: 16,384-body partially computed force can be paused; 1600x1000 PNG/SVG preserves the completed snapshot. A 128-body 8-step replay is identical.
print.criteria: Pause/export state unchanged, requested dimensions, all 16,384 SVG circles retained, deterministic completed positions.
print.limitations: One browser, selected dimensions and fixtures; CPU timing is hardware dependent and does not validate scientific accuracy.

domain.parameters: Planar Plummer-softened gravity with G=1; large-N force-kernel fixtures at N∈{256,1024,4096}, ε=0.12; moderate-N dt/ε band at N=64, t=0.4, ε∈{0.06,0.12,0.24} and h∈{0.004,0.002,0.001}; plus the small-orbit science pack and registered browser print fixtures.
domain.conditions: Equal-mass disk seed for regime tests; independent all-pairs Float64 force reference at fixed snapshot; wrong-G, ε×1.05, and broken-reciprocity controls must reject. Print: pause/export of completed 16,384-body snapshot and 128-body replay as registered.
domain.resolution: Force max |Δa| ~2e-15 / 5e-15 / 1e-14 at N=256/1024/4096; relative energy drift ~4.5e-6→2.8e-7 under h 0.004→0.001 (ratio ~16); position RMS refine ~5 on the ε band. Exact N/ε/h/steps recorded.
domain.precision: Float64 production kernel vs independent all-pairs reference; finite-time fixtures only — not galaxy equilibrium, unsoftened close encounters, or chaotic long-time accuracy.
